text:
alex: Heads up — ran a 16-node TP run and hit a weird scaling stall around step 1200, one rank timed out and the rest kept spinning.
maya: Can you paste the root logs? did it OOM or hang on allreduce?
alex: No OOM. Kernel selector picked an FP16-int8 mixed path on some ranks (weird) then we saw this in the driver: 
```
[rank=7] allreduce timeout after 31000 ms, pending fragments: 2
[rank=7] kvcache_lookup: miss seq=18432
[rank=7] selected kernel: fast_gemm_quantized_v2 (fallback path)
[rank=2] selected kernel: fp16_stream_gemm
```
ben: Hmm mixed kernel choices across ranks would change buffer shapes/padding. Could cause mismatch for our fragmented allreduce algorithm.
eva: Any recent changes to kernel routing? autotuner?
alex: We rolled the autotuner change yesterday that prefers quantized kernels when estimated memory < X. But this workload has long seq tails and variable microbatch sizes.
maya: Profiling snapshot (cudaprofile) shows rank7 waiting on recv for 28ms while compute finished earlier — overlap dropped to ~6% before the stall.
ben: That matches a KV cache eviction pattern I saw — if prefix cache gets evicted on some ranks it changes kv-length used for fused kernels which affects negotiated buffer sizes.
eva: tl;dr — kernel selection + kv-evict + microbatch skew => comm/compute misalignment => allreduce fragments out of expected alignment => timeout.
alex: Repro steps I used: `./run_tp --nodes=16 --tp=8 --batch=2 --seq=4096 --profile --autotune=on` and added `--kv-cache=enable`. Repro is flaky but hits ~30% of runs after warmup.
maya: Can we force consistent kernel selection across ranks as a mitigation? e.g., coordinator picks kernel_family per model/seq batch.
eva: Good short fix: coordinator broadcast kernel hint before run and disable per-rank autotune. Longer fix: make rendezvous validate fragment sizes before starting allreduce; fail-fast with trace id.
infra-bot: test-job-22765 requeued by infra (reason: job timed out on rank 7).
ben: For triage next: 1) capture kvcache hit/miss timeline per rank 2) add a debug trace at rendezvous to log negotiated fragment sizes 3) try forced-kernel run to check if stall disappears.
alex: I'll collect kvcache traces + full profile and kick off a forced-kernel experiment. Posting results in this thread once available. :thumbsup:
